Seminar Title:

Measuring the Effect of Artificial Intelligence Marketing Activities on Purchase and Resistance Intention: A Study of the E-commerce Industry

Seminar Type:

Defence Seminar

Department:

School of Management

Speaker Name:

Rajat Kukreti ( Rollno : 521sm1002)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Conference Room (SM)

Date and Time:

29 Oct 2026 01:00 PM

Contact:

Mayank Yadav

Abstract:

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed marketing by enabling organizations to deliver personalized, adaptive, and data-driven experiences throughout the consumer journey. Although the adoption of AI in e-commerce has accelerated considerably, existing research remains fragmented, lacks a comprehensive measure of AI-enabled marketing activities, and provides limited understanding of the simultaneous benefits and risks associated with AI-driven marketing. This thesis addresses these gaps through a comprehensive investigation of Artificial Intelligence Marketing (AIM) in the context of e-commerce. The research begins by systematically synthesizing the existing AIM literature using the ADO&ndashTCM framework and the SPAR-4-SLR protocol. By reviewing 114 peer-reviewed articles published between 2013 and 2025, it consolidates fragmented knowledge, reconciles contradictory findings, identifies dominant theories, contexts, and methodologies, and develops a priority&ndashfeasibility agenda to guide future research. Building on the insights from the review, the thesis conceptualizes and develops the Artificial Intelligence Marketing Activities (AIMA) construct and validates a multidimensional measurement scale following established scale development procedures involving qualitative exploration, expert validation, exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, and nomological validation. The validated scale comprises six dimensions: affinity, customization, information, interaction, problem-solving, and responsiveness, providing one of the first comprehensive measures of firm-initiated, consumer-viewable AI-enabled marketing activities in e-commerce. The thesis further examines how AIMA influences consumer behavior by proposing and empirically validating a dual-path framework grounded in the Stimulus&ndash Organism&ndashResponse framework, Psychological Ownership Theory, Attachment Theory, and Privacy Calculus Theory. The findings demonstrate that AIMA simultaneously creates value by enhancing consumer AI empowerment and psychological ownership while also generating vigilance through privacy concerns and threats to human identity, resulting in contrasting behavioral intentions. Overall, this thesis advances AIM literature by integrating fragmented knowledge, introducing a validated multidimensional scale for measuring AI-enabled marketing activities, and explaining the paradoxical effects of AI on consumer behavior. The findings offer important theoretical contributions and practical guidance for organizations seeking to design AI-enabled marketing strategies that enhance consumer experiences while addressing privacy and identity-related concerns in the rapidly evolving e-commerce environment.

Keywords: Artificial Intelligence Marketing Activities Consumer AI Empowerment Psychological Ownership Privacy Concerns Threat to Human Identity, E-commerce
